cite_as: MDRC (2026). Expanding High-Dosage Tutoring [evaluation of Saga Education's live-online tutoring model in eight New York City high schools, 2021-22 to 2023-24].
claimed_component: Design: quasi-experimental matched comparison (students in comparable NYC high schools). Population: New York City, 9th graders, 8 high schools. Program: Saga high-dosage math tutoring delivered live online. Outcome: NY State Algebra I Regents exam passing and score by end of 9th grade; math GPA. Direction: positive. Reported effect: MDRC page: 'Students who received tutoring using the model were more likely to pass the standardized state Algebra I Regents Exam by the end of ninth grade (39 percent compared with 31 percent for the comparison group), they had higher Regents Exam scores, and they earned higher math grade point averages'

cite_as: Bhatt, M. P., Guryan, J., Khan, S. A., LaForest-Tucker, M., & Mishra, B. (2024). Can Technology Facilitate Scale? Evidence from a Randomized Evaluation of High Dosage Tutoring. NBER Working Paper 32510.
claimed_component: Design: randomized controlled trial, ~4,000 students. Population: Two large districts (Chicago and New York City), 2018-19 and 2019-20, high school. Program: Saga hybrid tutoring: groups of four, 2 with in-person tutor and 2 on computer-assisted learning, alternating days. Outcome: Math standardized test scores. Direction: positive. Reported effect: NBER abstract: 'We find gains in students' math standardized test scores of 0.23 standard deviations for participating students'; per-pupil costs 'approximately 30 percent lower than the 2-to-1 tutoring model'

cite_as: Somers, M.-A., Corrin, W., Sepanik, S., Salinger, T., Levin, J., & Zmach, C. (2010). The Enhanced Reading Opportunities Study Final Report: The Impact of Supplemental Literacy Courses for Struggling Ninth-Grade Readers (NCEE 2010-4021). IES/MDRC. ERIC ED511811.
claimed_component: Design: RCT (students randomized within 34 high schools; schools randomized to program). Population: Grade 9 students reading 2-5 years below grade level; 34 high schools, 10 US districts; 2 cohorts (n=2,916 and 2,679). Program: Year-long supplemental literacy course replacing an elective (Reading Apprenticeship Academic Literacy or Xtreme Reading). Outcome: Reading comprehension (GRADE); state ELA and math tests where given in grade 9; core GPA; credits; grade 10 follow-up. Direction: positive in program year; null the following year. Reported effect: Fetched executive summary: comprehension ES 0.09; core GPA ES 0.07; core credits ES 0.06; 'students also scored higher on their English language arts and mathematics tests ... effect size of these impacts are 0.11 and 0.07'; in the following school year impacts on GPA, credits and state test scores 'are not statistically significant'.

cite_as: Vaughn, S., Roberts, G., Wexler, J., Vaughn, M. G., Fall, A.-M., & Schnakenberg, J. B. (2015). claimed_component: Design: RCT (four arms: reading, reading plus dropout prevention, dropout prevention only, business as usual). Population: Grade 9-10 students who failed the state accountability reading test, Texas. Program: Two-year daily small-group reading intervention in place of an elective. Outcome: Standardized reading comprehension; social studies grades. Direction: positive. cite_as: Baye, A., Inns, A., Lake, C., & Slavin, R. E. (2019). A Synthesis of Quantitative Research on Reading Programs for Secondary Students. Reading Research Quarterly, 54(2), 133-166. ERIC EJ1210152; EEF version ED612242.
claimed_component: Design: Meta-analysis of 69 studies (62 RCTs, 7 strong QEDs). Population: Secondary students grades 6-12, US and UK. Program: 51 programs; categories: tutoring, cooperative learning, whole-school, writing-focused, content-focused, strategies, technology. Outcome: Widely accepted standardized reading measures. Direction: positive for tutoring, cooperative learning, whole-school, writing-focused categories; extra reading periods and technology no better. Reported effect: Fetched EEF text: paid-adult tutoring weighted ES +0.24 (all 7 tutoring studies in England); volunteer TextNow ES -0.06; writing-focused +0.13; 27 extra-reading-period studies +0.09 vs 42 without +0.10; Reading Apprenticeship family +0.07.

cite_as: Herrera, S., Truckenmiller, A. J., & Foorman, B. R. (2016). Summary of 20 Years of Research on the Effectiveness of Adolescent Literacy Programs and Practices (REL 2016-178). REL Southeast. ERIC ED568684.

cite_as: Edmunds, J. A., Unlu, F., Glennie, E., Bernstein, L., Fesler, L., & Furey, J. (2017). Smoothing the transition to postsecondary education: The impact of the early college model. claimed_component: Design: lottery-based RCT (WWC: meets standards without reservations). Population: North Carolina early college high school applicants, grades 9-12. ERIC abstract: treatment students 'graduated from high school, enrolled in postsecondary education, and received postsecondary credentials at higher rates'.

cite_as: Olsen, R., Seftor, N., Silva, T., Myers, D., DesRoches, D., & Young, J. (2007). Upward Bound Math-Science: Program description and interim impact estimates. claimed_component: Design: matched comparison (UBMS participants vs. regular Upward Bound applicants matched on grade 9 GPA and course-taking); transcripts. Reported effect: Report (fetched): UBMS increased 'the average GPA in science courses from 2.7 to 2.9' and raised 'the percentage of students taking chemistry from 78 percent to 88 percent and ... physics from 43 percent to 58 percent'.

cite_as: Myers, D., Olsen, R., Seftor, N., Young, J., & Tuttle, C. (2004). The Impacts of Regular Upward Bound: Results from the Third Follow-Up Data Collection. Mathematica Policy Research for U.S. Department of Education. ERIC ED518667.
claimed_component: Design: Randomized controlled trial (national, nationally representative sample of projects). Population: US national; low-income / first-generation high school students. Program: Upward Bound (federal TRIO college-preparation program run by colleges and nonprofits: academic instruction, tutoring, summer residential program). Outcome: High school math credits; other measures of high school academic preparation (transcripts). Direction: mixed (math credits positive; other high school academics null). Reported effect: ERIC abstract: Upward Bound '(1) increased the number of high school math credits earned by participants; (2) did not affect other measures of high school academic preparation'

cite_as: Olsen, R., Seftor, N., Silva, T., Myers, D., DesRoches, D., & Young, J. (2007). Upward Bound Math-Science: Program Description and Interim Impact Estimates. Mathematica Policy Research for U.S. Department of Education. ERIC ED497631.

Outcome: High school grades in math, science and overall; taking chemistry and physics. Direction: positive. Reported effect: ERIC abstract: 'Major findings of the impact analysis for UBMS include: (1) Improved high school grades in math and science and overall; (2) Increased likelihood of taking chemistry and physics in high school'

cite_as: Leuwerke, W. C., Ingleby, L. D., Tillery, C. Y., Cech, T. G., & Sibaouih, C. M. (2021). Narrowing the College Readiness Gap: Assessing GEAR UP Iowa's Intermediate Impact on Underserved Students. Journal of Education for Students Placed at Risk. doi:10.1080/10824669.2021.1884864

cite_as: Merrill, L., Cole, R., Soltani, J., & Kang, D. (2017). iMentor's College Ready Program: Examining Implementation and Impacts for 10th Graders. Research Alliance for New York City Schools. ERIC ED591554. Final report: Merrill, L. (2020), ERIC ED609326.

cite_as: Zhu, P., Garcia, I., Boxer, K., Wadhera, S., & Alonzo, E. (2019). Using a Growth Mindset Intervention to Help Ninth-Graders: An Independent Evaluation of the National Study of Learning Mindsets. MDRC. ERIC ED601132.

cite_as: Liu, J., Lee, M., & Gershenson, S. (2021). The short- and long-run impacts of secondary school absences. Journal of Public Economics, 199, 104441. (EdWorkingPaper 19-125, ERIC ED671028.)

cite_as: Boulay, B., Goodson, B., Frye, M., Blocklin, M., & Price, C. (2015). Summary of Research Generated by Striving Readers on the Effectiveness of Interventions for Struggling Adolescent Readers (NCEE 2016-4001). IES. ERIC ED560732.
